verdicts.evidence: The ?? fires only when the manifest's last byte is a backslash inside a string, which leaves that string unterminated, so JSON.parse throws in both versions and the outcome is `unread` either way. Measured: 41 371 exhaustively enumerated JSONC documents gave zero difference in the JSON.parse OUTCOME, and two crafted truncated manifests plus 1 200 fuzzed ones gave identical Derivations.

verdicts.evidence: `i <= text.length` only lets the line-comment scan step one index past the end, where text[i] is undefined (never a newline) and the outer `while (i < text.length)` exits identically. Measured: 111 111 exhaustively enumerated JSONC documents over a 10-character alphabet gave byte-identical stripJsonc output, and 1 200 fuzzed manifests identical Derivations.

verdicts.evidence: At `i === text.length` the added iteration tests `text[i] === "*"` on undefined, which is false, so the scan stops one index later and the following `i += 2` lands past the end in both versions. Measured: 111 111 exhaustively enumerated documents byte-identical, plus 1 200 fuzzed manifests with identical Derivations and two crafted truncated-comment manifests.
